method: Actual reviewer reading of the four complete affected display answers and original Q1/Q7 task contexts, with independent physical reasoning against the immutable d613 criterion. Mechanical equality assertions supply preservation evidence, not scientific or linguistic judgment.

independent_scientific_evidence: At an ordinary stationary isotropic interface, equal tangential phase components give the fixed-frequency product-form Snell law. The first and last lines still restrict the indices to the same frequency and correctly distinguish transmission from reflection.

At exactly normal incidence, a zero incident angle makes the product law require a zero transmitted angle for positive indices. Both segments lie on the normal. The new second line expressly states this in both languages and confines the opposite-sides clause to oblique incidence.

At oblique incidence with a propagating transmitted ray, the incoming and outgoing geometrical segments lie on opposite sides of the normal in the incidence plane. The repaired qualification retains this usual construction rather than changing the law.
At normal incidence the incidence plane is not unique, but a plane containing the normal contains both collinear segments; the first-line coplanarity statement is not contradicted.

There is no ratio singularity, reflection-law substitution, invented numerical datum, or newly narrowed original question. The d613 qualification that a propagating transmitted ray is considered when it exists remains inherited, not replaced by a new total-internal-reflection task.

complete_context_checks.evidence: Fixed frequency, homogeneous isotropic transparent media, geometrical optics and coplanarity are retained and equivalently expressed.
Oblique/normal case split fixes the entire literal-domain defect; normal-reference angles and the unchanged Snell span remain paired.
Same-frequency indices and distinction from reflection remain correct and equivalent.

bilingual_evidence: The unchanged Chinese brief-law prompt and English laws-of-refraction prompt request the same conceptual response as the original.

The Chinese oblique-incidence and perpendicular-incidence wording corresponds to English oblique incidence and normal incidence; both state opposite sides only in the former case and lying on the normal in the latter.
Chinese names the two rays and English names both ray segments. Within the given geometrical-optics context this is equivalent, not an additional restriction or missing zero-angle case.
Coplanarity, the incidence-point normal, normal-referenced angles, fixed frequency and contrast with reflection remain aligned across all three lines.

evidence: RAW assumptions explicitly include normal incidence and RAW uses the product form rather than an undefined zero-over-zero ratio.

RAW also contains an unqualified opposite-sides clause in its derivation and explanation. This limitation is not accepted as an oracle; the repaired display sentence is tested against the normal-incidence reasoning independently.
No conclusion is drawn about RAW Q2,Q3,Q4,Q5,Q6,Q8 or blanket RAW correctness.

independent_scientific_evidence: In the inherited same-medium paraxial thin-lens model, the outgoing slope is the incoming slope reduced by the ray's lens-plane height divided by focal length. A line through the converging lens's object-side focus has exactly that incoming slope, so its outgoing ray is parallel whether or not the focus is on the actual incident segment.

For the original allowed inside-focus case, the positive real object distance is smaller than the converging focal length. The object lies between the focus and the lens, so the focus is behind the emitter. A nonaxial ray from that object to the lens can have a supporting line through the focus even though its physical segment never passes the focus. The explicit backward-extension clause now includes precisely this case in both languages.

The supporting-line description is also valid for virtual-object constructions. It does not invent a physical passage through a point outside the incoming segment or assert that backward extensions carry light.
The other two named converging-lens rays remain valid in the inherited approximation: a parallel input uses the image-side focus, and the optical-center ray has no directional change.

The unchanged diverging-lens sentence correctly distinguishes virtual image-focus backward extension from an input aimed at the outgoing-side object focus. It does not turn the original general lens question into a converging-only task.

The unchanged independent-ray condition locates finite real images by outgoing intersections and virtual images by backward intersections. For focal conjugates the usual finite-intersection prescription has its inherited infinity limit; no new finite-image or numerical case is asserted.

The axial-degeneracy warning remains correct. A nonaxial auxiliary direction and the corresponding image-side focal-plane point provide another line construction; d613's existing terse-clarity note remains nonblocking and is not converted into another author-repair request.

complete_context_checks.evidence: The listed trio is explicitly scoped to a converging thin lens, not inferred as a property of the original question.
Parallel input and image-side focus rule remain correct and equivalent.
Incident supporting line and backward extension remove the actual-before-lens restriction without changing the parallel output rule.
Optical-center direction remains unchanged within the thin-lens approximation.
Two independent lines, actual real-image intersections and backward virtual-image intersections remain paired.
The diverging virtual-focus extension and outgoing-focus aimed-input rules remain paired; the original nonblocking terminology note is retained.
Axial degeneracy, another nonaxial ray and focal-plane construction remain paired; coincident rays are not counted as independent.

bilingual_evidence: Both unchanged prompts preserve the original request to name convenient construction rays, not to produce a drawing for an invented object position.
The Chinese incident-ray-containing straight line means the same geometric supporting line as the English phrase, and both immediately include a backward extension through the object-side focus.
Both languages separate actual outgoing lines from backward construction extensions, preserving physical-path meaning.
Converging versus diverging lenses, object versus image focus, optical center, independent rays and on-axis degeneration retain the same conceptual roles across the complete seven-line contexts.

evidence: RAW uses the incident supporting line and recognizes that extension, rather than physical passage, is necessary in general.
Agreement with RAW alone is not the pass criterion. The repaired text is independently tested against the inherited inside-focus countercase and the paraxial slope rule.
RAW's broader axial wording and image-at-infinity assumption are comparison context only. No RAW or figure approval is issued.
